title: Librarian Salary: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to calculate your librarian salary from hourly rates, including award rates, casual loading, super, and tax. Use our timesheet for accurate estimates.

faqs.q: What is the typical hourly rate for a librarian in Australia?
faqs.a: According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (via Jobs and Skills Australia), the median hourly earnings for librarians are $48 per hour as of May 2025. This is for full-time non-managerial employees. However, actual rates vary by award classification, experience, and location. For example, the Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database sets minimum rates under the Library Employees Award, which are generally higher than the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect a librarian's pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For a librarian on the median $48 per hour, the casual rate would be $60 per hour. This loading compensates for lack of paid leave and other entitlements. Superannuation is calculated on the loaded rate. Use our timesheet with the casual loading checkbox to see the difference.

faqs.q: What tax and super should a librarian expect?
faqs.a: For the 2026–27 financial year, tax rates are: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is 2% (single thresholds not confirmed for 2026–27). Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a librarian earning $95,732 annually, super would add about $11,488 per year.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Librarian Salary

If you work in a library or are considering a career in the sector, knowing how to convert your hourly rate to an annual salary is essential. This guide explains the key components of a librarian salary in Australia, using the latest data from the Fair Work Commission, the Australian Bureau of Statistics, and the Australian Taxation Office.

### The National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, most librarians are covered by an award, such as the Library Employees Award or the Educational Services (Schools) General Staff Award. The Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database sets minimum rates for each classification. For example, a Library Technician at Level 4 may earn a higher minimum than the National Minimum Wage. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate, bringing the casual minimum to $33.05 per hour.

### Converting Hourly to Annual Pay

The standard formula for annual gross pay is:

**hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume 38 hours per week for full-time work. For a librarian earning the median hourly rate of $48 (from ABS data), the calculation is:

$48 × 38 × 52 = $94,848 per year

This aligns closely with the ABS-reported median full-time weekly earnings of $1,841, which annualises to $95,732. For part-time roles, adjust the hours per week accordingly. To find your fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly amount by 2.

### Casual Loading and Super

If you are a casual librarian, your base rate is increased by 25% casual loading. For example, a casual librarian on a $48 base rate would earn $60 per hour. Superannuation is calculated on ordinary earnings, which include the casual loading. The super guarantee is 12%, paid on top of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a full-time librarian earning $94,848, super adds about $11,382 per year.

### Tax Considerations

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- $190,001+: 45%

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (single thresholds not yet confirmed for 2026–27). For a librarian earning $94,848, the estimated tax (including Medicare) is around $22,000, leaving a take-home pay of about $72,800. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a personalised estimate.

### Using the Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) allows you to enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It calculates annual, fortnightly, and weekly amounts, including estimated super and tax. This is an estimate only – it assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. For award-specific rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Key Takeaways

- The median librarian salary is about $95,700 per year (38 hours/week) based on ABS data.
- Award minimum rates are higher than the National Minimum Wage.
- Casual loading adds 25% to the base rate.
- Super is 12% paid on top, and tax follows the 2026–27 resident scale.
- Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to check your own figures.

For more details on minimum wage, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page. To understand casual loading better, visit [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading). And for super and salary packaging, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).
